papers.title: Gene expression in the hypothalamus of gonad-sex chromosome divergent embryonic chickens
papers.abstract: Sexual differentiation of the brain of birds is shaped by gonadal steroid hormones and also by cell-autonomous mechanisms resulting from limited sex chromosome dosage compensation. In this study, we compare gene expression in the hypothalamus of gonad-sex chromosome divergent embryonic chickens treated with the aromatase inhibitor fadrozole to their control counterparts. Consistent with a lack of dosage compensation, we find a robust effect of sex chromosomes on hypothalamic gene expression, and a large portion of differentially expressed genes were on the Z and W sex chromosomes. Despite the presence of developing testes and markedly reduced estrogen concentrations in fadrozole-treated chromosomal female (ZW) birds, we find modest effects of gonadal hormones on gene expression in the brain. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis revealed that the most prominent effects were attributable to interactions between chromosomal sex and treatment. Our results highlight that chromosomal sex and steroid hormones together shape the sexual differentiation of the embryonic avian brain, challenging the primacy of the organizational effects of sex steroids on the brain during development.

papers.title: A radial glial regulatory program bridges progenitor maintenance and neuronal identity
papers.abstract: The cerebral cortex acquires its neuronal diversity through successive waves of neurogenesis. How molecular differences among early progenitors relate to their neuronal output remains unclear. Here, we identify a molecular program in early SOX9-high radial glia (S9RGs) that links progenitor maintenance with the regulation of genes associated with neuronal identity. Combining transcriptional and chromatin profiling with in vivo perturbations, we identify a program involving extracellular signaling, cell-cycle regulation, progenitor maintenance, and neurogenesis. We show that SOX9 regulates part of this program, including receptors that contribute to progenitor maintenance, while Notch acts upstream of Sox9 and reproduces several transcriptional and chromatin features of S9RGs. S9RGs express selected later-stage radial glial features and show distinct chromatin accessibility patterns at genes involved in progenitor maintenance, neurogenesis, and neuronal identity. Notch activation reproduces part of these changes, including differences at genes associated with lower- and upper-layer neuronal specification. Interestingly, S9RGs, which preferentially generate upper-layer neurons, share molecular features with the highly proliferative RG population in ferrets and with human outer RGs (oRGs) from cortical organoids, despite their different positions within the developing cortex. Together, our findings suggest that molecular differences among early radial glia could influence both how long they remain as progenitors and the neuronal identities they subsequently generate.

papers.title: Genetic, neural and early-environmental architecture of resilience
papers.abstract: Resilience is shaped by factors ranging from the genome through early-life experience to the brain, yet its biological basis in humans remains unclear because studies have rarely integrated these levels and have been confined to small samples. Using the Brief Resilience Scale (BRS) and multimodal data from tens of thousands of UK Biobank (UKB) participants, with replication in Generation Scotland (GS), we found that resting-state functional connectivity, particularly within the flexibility and valuation networks, is a robust neural correlate of resilience. Resilience also showed a generalizable genetic basis: a polygenic score (PGS) derived from a UKB genome-wide association study predicted BRS in GS. Genes and childhood experiences converged on the flexibility network through distinct routes: the polygenic association with resilience was partly explained by central executive-salience integration, whereas childhood experiences were associated with default-mode-centered integration. By separating genetically anchored from experience-sensitive routes, these findings point to network targets that interventions could tailor to the sources of an individual's vulnerability.

papers.title: Neural reactivation of past events tracks narrative understanding as it unfolds
papers.abstract: Understanding of episodic experience is not achieved at a single moment: it is a constructive process in which each new event is interpreted in light of relevant past events and prior knowledge. Yet this process is rarely measured as it unfolds, leaving unclear how the brain integrates past events to construct an evolving understanding of the present. We hypothesized that neural reactivation of past events at narrative event boundaries reflects not merely what people experience, but how they interpret their experience. We developed a behavioural paradigm that tracks, as a narrative unfolds, which past events people consider relevant for understanding each new event. By manipulating prior knowledge of the narrative's final plot twist, we examined the process by which the same experience yields different understanding. Across independent behavioural and fMRI cohorts, we found that prior knowledge similarly altered the variability and intersubject similarity of inferred relations between events and their neural reactivation at narrative event boundaries in the Default Mode Network. Moreover, stronger neural reactivation was associated with greater inferred relevance between events, and event pairs showing different behavioural relations across groups also showed corresponding differences in reactivation. These findings suggest that neural reactivation of past events at event boundaries reflects an unfolding inferential process that transforms shared experience into subjective understanding.

papers.title: A temporal atlas of TDP-43 interactions reveals persistent network remodelling beyond stress granule clearance
papers.abstract: Cytoplasmic aggregation of the nuclear protein TDP-43 is associated with several neurodegenerative disorders and may be promoted by cellular stress. However, the dynamics of TDP-43 protein-protein interactions during stress and recovery remain poorly understood. Here, we combined APEX2 proximity labelling with quantitative mass spectrometry to generate a temporal atlas of wild-type TDP-43 and pathology-mimicking TDP-43dNLS and TDP-43CTF variants. Interactomes were profiled across steady state, oxidative stress, and recovery. We reveal extensive state- and variant-dependent remodelling of TDP-43 interaction networks, uncovering distinct temporal interaction patterns throughout the stress response and recovery. Notably, distinct TDP-43 interaction signatures persisted after stress granule clearance, suggesting a molecular memory of stress. Together, our study establishes a comprehensive temporal resource for investigating TDP-43 interaction dynamics and provides a framework for understanding how stress-induced network alterations may contribute to TDP-43 proteinopathies.

papers.title: Context-dependent requirement for neutrophils in retinal regeneration
papers.abstract: Innate immune responses shape Muller glia (MG) reprogramming and retinal regeneration, yet the contribution of individual immune cell type remains poorly defined. Neutrophils enter the blood-retinal-barrier (BRB)-damaged retina within hours of injury, but their role in retinal regeneration is unknown. Here we report that neutrophils are required for the regenerative responses in needle-poked, but not NMDA-injured, zebrafish retinas. Pharmacological ablation of neutrophils with Erbb2 inhibitors suppresses MG proliferation, progenitor formation, and subsequent neuronal regeneration after stab injury, whereas neutrophil depletion has no significant effect in the BRB-intact NMDA model. We further show that Cxcl12-Cxcr4b signaling retains neutrophils at the stab injury site, and manipulating neutrophil retention correspondingly alters the regenerative responses. Mechanistically, neutrophils may modulate MG reprogramming and proliferation by regulating microglial reactivity and by secreting a regeneration-promoting factor Hb-egf. These data identify neutrophil as a previously unrecognized regulator of retinal regeneration and establish that their contribution is injury context-dependent.

papers.title: Cross-species phosphoproteomic mapping of mTORC1 signalling reveals RNA splicing regulation during neurodevelopment
papers.abstract: Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) regulates diverse cellular processes through its kinase activity and is essential for nervous system development. Although mTORC1 hyperactivation causes numerous neurodevelopmental disorders, its downstream targets in the developing nervous system remain poorly defined. Here, by profiling thousands of proteins and tens of thousands of phosphosites during the neurogenic phase in mouse and human models, we systematically define the proteomic and phosphoproteomic landscape downstream of mTORC1 during neurodevelopment. To facilitate community access, we developed PhosphoTargets, an interactive platform comprising protein and phosphoprotein expression data from mTORC1 models and patient tissue. We demonstrate the utility of this resource by identifying the deubiquitylating enzyme USP9X as a novel mTORC1 substrate and showing that mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of USP9X regulates human neural progenitor cell proliferation. Furthermore, integration with gene expression datasets reveals a new role for mTORC1 in the regulation of mRNA splicing. Together, these data provide a comprehensive resource for investigating mTORC1 signalling mechanisms and reveal novel processes through which mTORC1 regulates neurodevelopment.

papers.title: Intra-thalamic coordination maintains arousability in slow-wave sleep
papers.abstract: Slow-wave sleep preserves the capacity for spontaneous or stimulus-evoked awakening despite reduced responsiveness, yet how thalamic nuclei coordinate to preserve arousability remains unclear. We analysed six fMRI and EEG datasets spanning sleep, propofol anesthesia and unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS). During N2 and N3, centromedian (CM) and ventral posterolateral (VPL) nuclei showed convergent edge-community profiles and increased closed-loop intra-thalamic motifs, changes not observed during anesthesia or UWS. During N3, directed effective connectivity along CM[->]VPL[->]pulvinar (PUL) increased versus wakefulness and N2. Stronger CM[->]VPL and VPL[->]PUL connectivity covaried with greater N3 delta power, which was higher before awakening than before transitions to N2 and positively associated with three-month improvement in behavioural responsiveness in UWS. These findings identify a CM-VPL-PUL-centred pattern of intra-thalamic organization linked to preserved arousability during slow-wave sleep, extending accounts focused on individual nuclei and thalamocortical interactions.

papers.title: ACC Sulcal Morphology as a Neurodevelopmental Marker of Proactive and Reactive Cognitive Control among Adolescents
papers.abstract: Behavioral inhibition (BI) is an early temperament associated with higher risk for later anxiety. BI has been linked to variation in cognitive control, particularly proactive control, a crucial component of executive functions which involves monitoring one's own behavior and adapting that behavior to achieve a particular goal, which may help explain BI's association with elevated anxiety risk. Yet little is known about the neurobiology of cognitive control development among children with BI. Variation in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) sulcal pattern asymmetry, established prenatally and stable across development, is associated with individual differences in cognitive control. This preliminary study examined whether ACC sulcal symmetry is associated with BI, proactive and reactive control (measured via the AX-CPT) in adolescents. Structural T1-weighted MRI was acquired from 62 adolescents aged 12 to 15 years. ACC patterns in each hemisphere were classified as 'single type' or 'double parallel type' based on the presence of a paracingulate sulcus. Adolescents with symmetric ACC patterns showed lower proactive control (d' context; 2p = .091) and greater reactive control (BX probe interference effect; 2p = .119). These associations held even when tested within the same statistical model and were comparable in magnitude. ACC symmetry was not associated with BI, nor did it interact with BI to predict cognitive control scores. Overall, the findings provide preliminary evidence that ACC sulcal morphology may be a structural marker of variability in cognitive control, with relevance to BI-related neurocognitive risk.

papers.title: No allocentric distractor-location learning following self-movement even with contextual anchors and explicit knowledge
papers.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires learning where relevant information can likely be found, but also where distraction is likely to occur. For such learning to be useful in everyday life, it must generalize across changing viewpoints as observers move through the environment. Recent work suggests a striking asymmetry in this regard: whereas target-location learning can be grounded in world-centered coordinates, distractor-location learning appears tied to the observer's current viewpoint. One possibility is that allocentric distractor-location learning requires stronger contextual support than allocentric target-location learning. Alternatively, distractor suppression may be fundamentally constrained by viewer-centered spatial coding. To distinguish between these possibilities, participants performed an additional-singleton search task displayed on a tabletop and continuously changed their standing position around the table, while the high-probability distractor location remained fixed in the external environment. Unlike previous studies using this paradigm, contextual anchors were embedded directly within the search display, allowing distractor locations to be encoded relative to a stable task-relevant allocentric structure. In a second experiment, participants were additionally explicitly informed about the distractor-location regularity. Despite task-relevant contextual structure and explicit knowledge, distractor-location learning failed to emerge in world-centered coordinates. Together with previous findings showing robust egocentric distractor-location learning using the same set-up, these findings strengthen the view that learned distractor suppression relies primarily on viewer-centered spatial coding, potentially reflecting a process linked to viewpoint-specific action selection.

papers.title: Glutamate/GABA Resource Asymmetry Enables Bidirectional Activity Correction
papers.abstract: Glutamate/GABA cotransmission allows one neuron to excite and inhibit the same target. How the two release branches translate a shared spike train into net synaptic drive, and how this drive shapes neural circuit activity, remain unclear. We introduce BRIDGE, a model with separate glutamate and GABA resources that deplete and recover under shared input. The model reproduced glutamatergic depression during repeated stimulation in cotransmission recordings. Late GABAergic responses showed weaker frequency dependence. This asymmetry can generate negative differential gain in the model, allowing faster presynaptic firing to weaken net drive while output remains excitatory. In simulated circuits, cotransmitting neurons shifted their output toward excitation when activity fell and toward inhibition when it rose, improving recovery after perturbations across all circuit sizes tested. Compared with baseline, a simplified spiking implementation yielded higher mean accuracy in most classification comparisons and lower error in selected prediction tasks. Thus, resource asymmetry links firing history to bidirectional correction of circuit activity.

papers.title: Rest promotes microglial clearance of degenerating neurons
papers.abstract: How the brain coordinates the removal of degenerating neurons with host rest and activity remains poorly understood. Using longitudinal two-photon imaging in mice with cytosolic TDP-43 proteinopathy, we show that microglia remove neuronal corpses through an ordered sequence of reaching, approaching, isolating and digesting. Clearance was higher during the light (resting) phase and lower during the dark (active) phase. This pattern reversed after light-dark cycle inversion and was blunted by sleep disruption. Chemogenetic inhibition of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons increased engulfment during the active phase, while activation and inhibition of the {beta}2-adrenergic receptor ADRB2 suppressed and enhanced clearance, respectively, identifying noradrenergic signaling as a brake on engulfment. However, sustained microglial ADRB2 deletion impaired clearance and blunted light-dark differences. These findings reveal that microglial removal of degenerating neurons is enhanced during rest and support a role for noradrenergic signaling in coordinating this cellular maintenance process with the host's rest-activity cycle.

papers.title: Reduced Resting Brain Entropy and Structural-Functional Reorganization in Hearing Loss
papers.abstract: Hearing loss changes how the brain processes sound, yet how chronic auditory degradation shapes the temporal organization of spontaneous cortical activity remains unclear. We examined this question using multimodal MRI from 52 adults with age-related hearing loss and 30 normal-hearing controls. Guided by convergent neuroimaging evidence, we focused on the superior temporal gyrus (STG) and assessed brain entropy (BEN), complementary resting-state measures, and gray matter volume (GMV). Hearing loss was associated with lower BEN in a focal right-STG cluster after adjustment for local GMV (14 voxels; cluster FWER p = 0.008), consistent with more recurrent BOLD signal patterns. Six complementary measures of signal amplitude, local synchrony, symbolic sequence diversity, successive variation, and temporal persistence showed no corrected STG differences. A separate whole-brain analysis revealed higher bilateral midcingulate cortex (MCC) GMV (FWE p = 0.002 and 0.015), motivating examination of the auditory-cingulate relationship. The BEN-defined STG region showed stronger focal functional connectivity with MCC (FWE p = 0.031). Exploratory analyses suggested weaker directed STG-to-MCC influence alongside a small tractography-derived group difference. Exploratory directional comparisons indicated stronger right-MCC GMV-BEN coupling (p = 0.034) and STG-MCC SC-FC coupling (p = 0.037) in controls than in hearing loss. Together, these findings link greater temporal regularity in auditory association cortex to altered auditory-cingulate coordination and local structure-function correspondence, suggesting that adaptation to hearing loss involves both the organization of spontaneous cortical dynamics and their relationship to brain structure.

papers.title: Social Connection: Resting-State Functional Connectivity Associations with Social Networks, and the Roles of Empathy and Sex
papers.abstract: Smaller social networks (SNs) negatively influence cognition, psychiatric trajectories and mortality. Studies linking SNs to resting-state functional connectivity (FC) inconsistently suggest orbito-frontal and frontoparietal regions and implicate a potential role for empathy and sex. We investigate how SN characteristics relate to FC, additionally assessing if empathy and sex alter these associations. Group-independent component analysis was applied to multi-band resting-state fMRI from 83 participants (Caltech Conte dataset: ds003798). The Social Network Index measures SN-contacts (SN-contacts) SN-diversity (number of roles) and SN-embeddedness (number of contact groups) and the Empathy Quotient measured empathy. Using MANCOVA, we investigate if resting-state network power and connectivity are associated with SNI measures and whether these relationships differ by empathizing ability and sex. Participants aged 18-48 (mean age 29.3+/-7.0, 55% male) demonstrated SN-contacts and SN-diversity associated with lower frontal-pole FC within the default-mode network (DMN, q-values<0.05). Empathy altered how SN-diversity and SN-contacts relate to superior lateral-occipital, default mode and salience network FC (q-values<0.05). Finally, males and females showed diverging associations of SN-contacts and SN-diversity with salience network power. Smaller SNs were associated with increased anterior-DMN FC, potentially indicating a tendency towards internally-directed cognition in more socially isolated individuals. Opposing relationships between SNs with salience and lateral-frontoparietal networks by empathy level highlights empathy as critical for understanding social biology. Males and females differed in SN associations with salience network coherency, supporting known sex-specific neural correlates of social behavior. These findings provide insights into the biology of social networks, offering potential targets for studying social deficits in psychiatric populations.

papers.title: Partial microglial depletion attenuates Purkinje cell degeneration and reshapes both glial and inflammatory responses in a mouse model of selective neurodegeneration
papers.abstract: Background The microglial population contributes to the inflammatory environment during neurodegeneration. Its role in neuronal loss remains hard to distinguish from its response to injury. We investigated how early pharmacological reduction of this population affects Purkinje cell preservation, behaviour and the cerebellar glial response. Methods We administered PLX5622 to Purkinje cell degeneration (PCD) and wild-type (WT) mice from postnatal day (P) 15 to P24 and compared them with their respective untreated controls. We assessed motor coordination, spontaneous behaviours and novel-object recognition at P17, P21 and P25. At P25, we quantified regional Purkinje cell preservation, glial immunoreactivity and microglial abundance and morphology. We assessed selected transcripts in whole-cerebellum samples by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Results At P25, treated PCD mice showed better motor coordination, improvements in selected spontaneous behaviours and greater novel-object discrimination. Greater Purkinje cell preservation coincided with lower glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) immunoreactivity in lobes IV-V and VIII. Microglial density decreased in all four PCD regions analysed. The territory encompassed by the processes of residual microglia expanded in both genotypes. In PCD mice, CD68-positive tissue area decreased in lobes I-II and IV-V, and the proportion of Iba1-positive area occupied by CD68 decreased in IV-V. CD45, CD16/32 and CD206 immunoreactivity decreased alongside selective reductions in immune, inflammatory and phagocytosis-associated transcripts. Treated WT mice showed early behavioural changes, including reduced novel-object discrimination. Conclusions Early PLX5622 treatment can modify the outcome of genetically driven cerebellar degeneration in PCD mice. The benefits achieved with partial microglial depletion provide a preclinical rationale for testing how the timing and extent of glial modulation influence neuronal protection during active degeneration.

papers.title: Whole-bulb LSFEM enables automated reconstruction and quantitative spatial mapping of thousands of olfactory glomeruli
papers.abstract: The glomerular layer of the olfactory bulb (OB) transforms chemical information into the first spatially organized neural representation of odor identity. Yet its three-dimensional architecture remains difficult to quantify at whole-bulb scale. Here, we establish an end-to-end framework integrating light-sheet fluorescence expansion microscopy (LSFEM) with automated reconstruction of thousands of individual glomeruli across intact mouse OBs. LSFEM preserves whole-bulb architecture and supports genetically encoded fluorescence and immunolabelling, providing continuous multichannel input for automated analysis. SegFormer-based segmentation of 2D optical sections was followed by morphology-guided separation and three-dimensional object reconstruction. Across 12 intact bulbs, the workflow yielded a median of 2,677 glomeruli per bulb, approaching the 2,851 reported by complete three-dimensional reconstruction. Object-level maps further revealed that glomeruli spanning a broad range of volumes were intermingled throughout the bulb without evident size-defined anatomical domains. Because each reconstructed glomerulus retains a three-dimensional centroid coordinate, the resulting object map can additionally be used as a specimen-specific spatial reference framework, allowing distances and distributions to be expressed relative to defined glomerular or anatomical positions within the intact OB. Together, whole-bulb LSFEM and automated reconstruction provide a scalable framework for quantitative three-dimensional mapping of glomerular number, morphology, and spatial organization, and the relative positioning of additional anatomical signals within the glomerular architecture.

papers.title: Whole-mount three-dimensional imaging and quantitative analysis platform for early brain development using dorsal forebrain spheroids
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional culture systems have emerged as a bridge between in vitro and in vivo models. Organoids and spheroids derived from human stem cells can model cellular interactions, morphology and organization of the neocortex, and provide a platform for future translational research into neurological disorders. However, the heterogeneity commonly found in 3D culture systems presents considerable challenges for identifying significant, reproducible, and disorder-relevant phenotypes. Here, we present a rigorous methodological framework for the longitudinal analysis of dorsal forebrain spheroids, beginning with gross spheroid morphology, extending to structural phenotypes in rosette morphogenesis, and culminating in cellular analyses of neural progenitor cell proliferation and cell cycle dynamics. This workflow integrates isogenic iPSC-derived spheroid culture, whole-mount optical clearing, high-resolution 3D imaging and reconstruction, and cumulative EdU-labeling assays. Testing the sensitivity of this approach in an isogenic Down syndrome model, we reliably detected new features of altered spheroid growth, delayed rosette emergence, reduced rosette density, and prolonged progenitor cell cycle progression. This approach provides a reproducible strategy for measuring complex developmental phenotypes in 3D culture models and can be applied to neurodevelopmentally altered cell lines beyond Down syndrome.

papers.title: Adaptation can explain cortical responses to sound deviance without requiring prediction
papers.abstract: Sensory systems amplify what is rare, allowing animals to orient toward threats and opportunities hidden among regular events. Whether this deviance detection reflects neuronal adaptation or error against the brain's predictive model is debated. The two processes can contribute simultaneously because the context that enables prediction also drives adaptation. To dissociate them, we recorded from primary auditory cortex neurons in awake mice during a modified oddball paradigm that separated recent sound history from longer-term sequence statistics. Contextual effects ranged from suppression to facilitation of responses. Facilitation increased with deviance magnitude, as expected for prediction error. However, neither facilitation, suppression, nor stimulus-specific adaptation depended on these longer-term statistics. A normalization model in which a neuron's inputs adapt at different rates reproduced the range of contextual effects and their weakening in background noise. Adaptive normalization can therefore generate deviance signals, including facilitation, without requiring a predictive model.

papers.title: Integrating multiple imputation with harmonization in multisite neuroimaging data: implications for site effects and biological inference
papers.abstract: Multisite neuroimaging harmonization in Alzheimer's disease research with missing data has received limited attention in the literature. Here, we evaluated the performance of several harmonization methods in conjunction with multiple imputation (MI) to address missing data, using baseline [18F]flortaucipir tau positron emission tomography (PET) data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). We compared complete case and MICE-imputed datasets (m = 5) across the original ADNI-preprocessed data and four statistical harmonization approaches: ComBat with and without covariates, quantile normalization, and quantile regression. Weighted average standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) across six Braak regions were analyzed for each dataset-method combination. We assessed harmonization effectiveness using covariate-adjusted intraclass correlation coefficients and site-level pairwise differences, and evaluated biological effect preservation using Hedges' g, regression coefficients, and statistical significance for comparisons between cognitively impaired and unimpaired participants. For imputed analyses, effect sizes and regression coefficients were pooled using Rubin's rules, with statistical inference based on the pooled estimates. Post-processing harmonization reduced site-level variability compared to the original data, with method performance varying across evaluation metrics, while overall harmonization quality remained comparable after MI. Disease group differences remained statistically significant across all combinations, exhibiting a consistent regional pattern, strongest in Braak I and weakest in Braak VI. MI modestly increased effect size and coefficient estimates, with improved precision reflected by median standard error ratios below 1 (0.89 for effect sizes and 0.93 for coefficients). These findings indicate that integrating MI with harmonization preserves disease group differences and improves statistical efficiency without compromising harmonization performance, supporting a practical framework for multisite neuroimaging studies.

papers.title: Zona incerta drives a strategy of persistence during nocturnal predatory hunting in mice.
papers.abstract: Prey capture in lab mice is a complex, ethologically relevant behavior that provides us with an opportunity to study how mice integrate internal and external cues to drive goal-directed behaviors. Previous research has established that key parts of this behavior, such as the approach, are visually guided, but it has remained unknown how mice would perform if given exposure to hunting without visual cues. Zona incerta, a potential key locus for the integration of external and internal information, has previously been shown in naive mice to improve prey capture ability by increasing appetitive drive through integrating prey-related sensory information. It remains an open question if this region plays the same role in mice experienced with hunting in both the light and dark. Therefore, we examined the behavioral strategies used by mice with prior experience hunting in both the light and dark, as well as how these strategies are modulated by zona incerta. In experienced mice, we found that mice adjust their strategies to maintain similar success rates with and without visual cues, and that zona incerta further refines these strategies, specifically in the dark. This suggests that the role of zona incerta in these experienced mice is to maintain successful hunting by shifting behavioral strategies under ambiguous sensory conditions.

papers.title: Multisensory brain processing is associated with depressive symptoms in youth with chronic pain
papers.abstract: Juvenile fibromyalgia (JFM) is a chronic pain condition marked by widespread musculoskeletal pain and often accompanied by physical fatigue, nonrestorative sleep, headaches, anxiety, and depression. Previous studies have found that adolescents with fibromyalgia report augmented unpleasantness and altered brain responses to non-painful multisensory stimuli. Likewise, research in major depression has shown altered neural processing of sensory stimulation. We examined whether augmented brain responses to non-painful multisensory stimulation is associated with depressive symptoms in adolescent girls with JFM. Forty-six female adolescents with JFM (mean - SD, 16.43 - 1.10 years [range 13-18 years]) and 44 healthy participants (mean - SD, 16.09 - 1.06 years [range 13-18 years]) completed validated questionnaires assessing daily-life sensory hypersensitivity and depressive symptoms, alongside undergoing a functional MRI multisensory task. JFM patients reported significantly higher sensory unpleasantness than healthy participants, and this hypersensitivity was positively associated with depressive symptoms. Neuroimaging results in chronic pain patients revealed that greater depressive symptomatology was associated with increased activation in the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) (pFWE<0.05), a region implicated in self-referential processing and specifically rumination in adults with chronic pain. JFM patients showed increased PCC-left middle temporal gyrus task-dependent connectivity using psychophysiological interactions analysis (PPI). Furthermore, hyperconnectivity between the PCC and brain areas involved in cognitive-affective regulation, sensory integration, and memory processing was strongly correlated with depressive symptoms in JFM patients. These findings underscore the role of depressive symptoms in sensory processing and integration in JFM patients and highlight the complex interplay between sensory processing and emotional/self-referential brain function in patients.

papers.title: MK-6240
papers.abstract: Flortaucipir and MK-6240 are two tau imaging agents currently in use for measuring neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) progression in Alzheimers disease (AD). The aims of this study were to use postmortem AD and Down syndrome (DS) brain sections to study three issues: (1) Measure binding affinity of flortaucipir and MK-6240 in AD brain sections by using [125I]IPPI; (2) Evaluate the binding characteristics of [18F]flortaucipir in AD, DS and cognitively normal (CN) brains sections and compare them with [18F]MK-6240, and (3) Assess the binding of [18F]flortaucipir in CN and Parkinsons disease (PD) brain sections to identify any off-target binding. The half-maximal inhibition (IC50) of [125I]IPPI bound to anterior cingulate (AC) in AD brain sections for flortaucipir was 2.91 nM and MK-6240 was 5.99 nM. Using frontal cortex (FCX) and temporal cortex (TCX) of AD, DS and CN brain sections, [18F]flortaucipir displayed high levels of binding in the gray matter (GM) of AD and DS. The average ratio of DSAD GM to CN GM was 15.7 in FCX, while DSAD GM to CN GM was 15.2 for the TCX. In the case of AD, average ratio of AD GM to CN GM was 12.4 in FCX, while AD GM to CN GM was 9.5 for the TCX. Binding of [18F]flortaucipir in brain section of AC from CN and PD cases did not exhibit any off-target binding to monoamine oxidase-A (MAO-A). In summary, both flortaucipir and MK-6240 exhibit similar high affinity to tau and [18F]flortaucipir exhibits higher binding compared to [18F]MK-6240 in DSAD.

papers.title: Automated, high-throughput kinematic analysis of skilled reaching in rodent models of neurological injury
papers.abstract: Neurological dysfunction can diminish quality of life by disrupting the movement capacity required to accomplish tasks. Kinematic studies guide treatment development by revealing subtle relationships between patterns of movement and neurological dysfunction. However, these studies produce a large quantity of opaque, multifaceted, and often highly correlated data. Here we present a novel and efficient approach to collecting, analyzing, and interpreting kinematic data with high throughput. We automated a single pellet reaching task in mice and created a video analysis pipeline that scores task success and extracts kinematic features from reaches. To analyze the resulting data, principal component analysis was first applied to group covarying measurements into a few overarching dimensions of behavior. Regularized regression was then applied separately to select reach qualities that best predicted task success. Applied to four nervous system injury models, this approach revealed differences in the effects of injury type and rehabilitative intervention on movement patterns that were not apparent from task success alone.

papers.title: Brain Signal Variability and Brain-Behavior Coupling in Adults with Dyslexia
papers.abstract: Background: Brain signal variability indexed by fMRI has emerged as a promising transdiagnostic biomarker for neurodevelopmental disorders, demonstrating better predictive utility than time-averaged metrics for diagnosis, yet it remains underexplored in adult dyslexia. The Neural Noise Hypothesis of dyslexia proposes that genetic risk disrupts cortical excitation/inhibition balance, elevating neural noise and affecting processes essential for reading. Here, we examine resting-state fMRI BOLD variability, a metric linked to neural noise, in adults with dyslexia and investigate its links with behavior. Methods: In 30 adults with dyslexia (DY) and 76 typical readers (TR), we computed three complementary BOLD variability metrics: standard deviation (SD) and mean squared successive differences (MSSD) to quantify BOLD amplitude fluctuations, and dynamic regional homogeneity (dReHo) to quantify local temporal coordination. Voxel-wise group comparisons and partial least squares correlation analyses examined brain-behavior associations across a comprehensive behavioral battery spanning reading (e.g., word reading, phonological processing), math, oral language, working memory, and executive function domains. Results: DY showed higher SD and MSSD in the left ventral occipitotemporal pathway and higher MSSD in the cerebellum, whereas TR showed higher dReHo in frontal and temporoparietal regions. SD/MSSD in visual, somatomotor, cerebellar, and subcortical networks significantly covaried with multi-domain behavioral profiles. Conclusions: Adults with dyslexia showed localized, metric-specific differences in brain signal variability and brain-behavior covariance, indicating region-specific rather than global alterations. These results suggest that brain signal variability is a promising candidate task-free phenotype that could potentially index target engagement in interventions for adult dyslexia.

papers.title: Electrophysiological dynamics of empathy for self- and other-related pain
papers.abstract: Empathy requires the ability to generate shared representations of the self and others while maintaining a distinction between them. However, it remains unclear whether, and to what extent, the neural processes involved in sharing and understanding others' pain overlap with those involved in processing one's own pain, particularly with respect to their temporal dynamics. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying empathic processing of self- and other-related painful facial expressions. To this end, EEG signals were recorded from 42 female participants while they viewed self- and other-related painful and neutral expressions. During the early stage of processing, the difference in N2 amplitude between self-related and other-related stimuli was smaller in the painful than in the neutral condition. Nevertheless, self-related painful stimuli continued to elicit more negative N2 amplitudes and greater Alpha/Mu suppression than other-related painful stimuli. In contrast, during the late stage of empathic processing, no distinction was observed between self- and other-related painful stimuli. Instead, painful expressions, regardless of whether they were self- or other-related, elicited larger late positive potential (LPP) amplitudes. These findings suggest that empathic processing is characterized by an early self-other distinction followed by a later convergence in the neural representation of self- and other-related pain.

papers.title: Delayed Reduction in Painful Sensations Evoked by Cervical tSCS Following High-Frequency Stimulation
papers.abstract: Objective: Transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (tSCS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique with potential effects on pain perception. However, tSCS itself can evoke discomfort or pain at higher current intensities, and it remains unclear whether high-frequency tSCS alters the pain evoked by subsequent low-frequency stimulation. This study examined whether high-frequency cervical tSCS delivered at motor-threshold intensity is followed by changes in pain ratings elicited by low-frequency tSCS in healthy participants. Approach: Twenty-five healthy participants completed a single experimental session. Individual sensory, motor, and pain thresholds were determined using single-pulse tSCS at the C6-C7 spinal level. Pain was assessed using 1-Hz stimulation delivered for 1 min at an individually defined intensity corresponding to 6-7 points on a 0-10 Numerical Rating Scale. Participants then received 80-Hz tSCS for 10 min at motor-threshold intensity, followed by three repeated pain-assessment sessions separated by 5-min intervals. Surface electromyography was recorded from the flexor carpi radialis and extensor carpi radialis. Pain analysis included 25 participants, whereas EMG analysis included 18 participants. Main results: Pain ratings were significantly lower than baseline during the second and third post-stimulation assessments. In contrast, ratings obtained immediately after high-frequency stimulation did not differ significantly from baseline. EMG responses showed substantial inter-participant variability. No EMG metric showed a significant omnibus session effect after correction for multiple comparisons, although exploratory comparisons indicated transient increases in ECR AUC and mean rectified amplitude immediately after high-frequency stimulation. Significance: These findings indicate that high-frequency cervical tSCS can exert a measurable short-term influence on pain perception. Pain ratings and stimulation-evoked EMG responses showed different temporal patterns and represent complementary, non-equivalent outcomes of spinal stimulation.

papers.title: Age and Sex Differences in Lateral Ventricle Choroid Plexus Volume in a Large, Manually Segmented, Multi-Site MRI Dataset
papers.abstract: Introduction The choroid plexus (ChP), which produces cerebrospinal fluid and forms the blood-CSF barrier, has drawn growing interest in psychiatric and neurodegenerative neuroimaging. However, prior volumetric studies have relied largely on automated segmentation tools such as FreeSurfer, which show poor agreement with manual tracing, and have been limited to small, narrow-age, single-site samples. Methods We present DataPlex, a manually segmented lateral ventricle ChP dataset comprising 700 3T T1-weighted MRI scans drawn from 35 study/site categories, spanning a wide range of age, sex, and scanner manufacturer (GE, Philips, Siemens). Using generalized least squares models accounting for within-site dependence, we examined associations between ChP and lateral ventricle (LV) volume, and age, sex, scanner manufacturer, image resolution, a registration-based quality-control metric, intracranial volume, and cognitive performance. Results ChP volume displayed a positive linear association with age and was significantly greater in males than females, while LV volume showed a significant nonlinear relationship with age and no sex difference. Scanner manufacturer and image resolution were significantly associated with measured left LV volume but not with ChP volume, and the quality-control metric was not significantly associated with any outcome. Both ChP and LV volume were significantly associated with several cognitive domains, including emotion recognition, working memory, inhibitory control, and episodic memory. Conclusion These findings demonstrate meaningful differences in ChP volume across age and sex. DataPlex represents the largest demographically and technically diverse manually segmented ChP dataset to date, establishing reference benchmarks for future automated segmentation tools and underscoring the importance of accounting for demographic and technical covariates in choroid plexus research.

papers.title: Scaling up naturalistic narrative research: A reproducible large language model-based tool for evaluating contextual information gain
papers.abstract: Narratives are a universal part of natural human experience. As experimental stimuli, narratives allow scientists to study complex mental processes with direct relevance to everyday experience. These analyses typically require manual labeling of key event features. Such characterization of narrative stimuli are extremely labor-intensive and prone to subjectivity. Automated tools could reduce these difficulties and enable scaling to longer, varied stimuli by exposing the exact quantities computed. We address this by introducing a metric that uses open-weight LLMs to compute contextual information gain. Our metric correlates with human ratings of event importance and causal centrality, critically distinguishing the latter from semantic centrality, thus overcoming limitations of existing automated tools. The metric similarly captures shared coactivation in the default mode network, a network implicated in narrative comprehension. Taken together, these results validate an automated, empirically-grounded tool that researchers can use to identify behaviorally- and neurally-relevant computational quantities in naturalistic stimuli.

papers.title: Age-associated skeletal muscle dysfunction with spinal cord pathology in an App knock-in model of Alzheimer's disease
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is increasingly recognized in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its pathological basis remains poorly understood. We examined age-associated muscle dysfunction together with skeletal muscle and spinal motor system alterations in male AppNL-G-F/NL-G-F knock-in (App-KI) mice, which develop age-dependent amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) pathology without amyloid precursor protein (APP) overexpression. Middle-aged, but not adult, App-KI mice showed lower strength-related performance than age-matched wild-type mice, whereas skeletal muscle mass and myofiber cross-sectional area were preserved. General motor performance was also preserved, suggesting that the strength-related impairment did not simply reflect generalized motor dysfunction. Middle-aged App-KI mice had higher percentages of centrally nucleated fibers in the gastrocnemius and quadriceps femoris muscles. Transcriptomic and targeted expression analyses further revealed alterations in molecular profiles related to muscle development and myosin, including reduced expression of factors involved in myoblast fusion and selected myosin proteins. Despite evident cerebral A{beta} pathology, no apparent A{beta} immunoreactivity was detected in skeletal muscle. In the lumbar ventral horn, App-KI mice had fewer choline acetyltransferase-positive motor neurons, greater A{beta} deposition, and increased immunoreactivity for glial fibrillary acidic protein and ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1; serum interleukin-6 levels were also selectively elevated in middle-aged App-KI mice. Together, these findings indicate that age-associated reductions in strength-related performance in App-KI mice occur without overt muscle atrophy and are accompanied by histological and molecular abnormalities in skeletal muscle and pathological changes in the lumbar spinal cord. Thus, AD-related physical dysfunction may involve abnormalities in both peripheral skeletal muscle and the spinal motor system.

papers.title: Elucidating the Sodium Channel-Targeting Anti-Seizure Medication Interactome: A Drug-Target Pathway Analysis
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder in both children and adults, primarily managed with anti-seizure medications (ASMs). Sodium channel blockers are among the most commonly used ASMs. These medications exhibit distinct spectra of efficacy and side effect profiles. These likely result from different off-target interactions, protein binding profiles, and subunit selectivity that remain poorly characterized. We developed a neural network-based computational pipeline to systematically elucidate the molecular targets and associated biological pathways of selected sodium channel-modulating ASMs: carbamazepine, lamotrigine, eslicarbazepine, licarbazepine, lacosamide, phenytoin, and cenobamate. Using the DRIFT (Drug-target identification based on chemical similarity) algorithm for proteome-wide target prediction, we identified protein targets for these ASMs. The sodium channel alpha subunit family was the highest-ranked target for every drug except cenobamate, for which it ranked second behind the GABA-A receptor. Pathway mapping in the Reactome database revealed both shared and drug-specific biological processes. Furthermore, molecular docking studies elucidated the atomistic interactions between the drugs and the predicted targets. Specifically, the predicted target landscape varied from eslicarbazepine and licarbazepine (59 predicted targets each) to lacosamide (18). Pathway analysis revealed recurrent enrichment in rapid depolarisation and the interaction between L1 and ankyrins shared across all drugs, alongside predicted off-targets, including the cannabinoid CB1 receptor for phenytoin and the carbonic anhydrases for lacosamide. Molecular docking supported these predictions, with binding scores ranging from -24 to -31 kcal/mol. Overall, this work provides a systems-level view of NaV-targeting ASM pharmacology and a hypothesis-generating framework to prioritize mechanistic and combination studies of these medications in epilepsy.
